heroHeadline: PLA 7 Sorties (5 Cross Median Line Into N/SW ADIZ); USTR Greer Contradicts Trump — 'No Change in US Policy' on Arms; Taiwan Excluded From WHO for 10th Year; HIMARS Deadline 13 Days
heroSubtitle: PLA activity ticked up on May 18: 7 aircraft sorties with 5 crossing the median line into northern and southwestern ADIZ sectors, up from 6 sorties (4 crossing) on May 17 — continuing post-Trump-Xi summit moderate-pressure operations. The diplomatic landscape shifted significantly when US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer publicly contradicted President Trump's 'bargaining chip' framing, stating there is 'no change in American policy' on Taiwan arms sales. This intra-administration incoherence — with Rubio calling arms discussions something that 'did not feature prominently' and Trump calling the $14B PAC-3/NASAMS package 'in abeyance' as a 'very good negotiating chip' — leaves Taiwan's security equation in institutional limbo. President Lai Ching-te reiterated on May 17-18 that Taiwan 'will not relinquish its national sovereignty and dignity' and invoked TSMC's ~72% global foundry share as a shared US-Taiwan strategic interest independent of any arms negotiation. On the same day, the 79th World Health Assembly opened in Geneva and Taiwan was excluded for the tenth consecutive year, drawing condemnation from the US and EU. The HIMARS payment deadline (May 31) is now 13 days away; the KMT-inserted procedural LOA approval requirement remains the critical bottleneck. Full May PLA sortie sequence: 4→29→1→2→1→0→22→12→8→12→7→9→2→3→15→6→7.
